expectations.text: The agent explains that ContentUnpublishedNotification fires after the page has been removed from the published cache, so GetById returns null and nothing is recorded
expectations.evidence: Response section 'The cause: wrong notification' explicitly states: 'ContentUnpublishedNotification, the "-ed" notification. In Umbraco 17 that notification fires after the unpublish has finished and the page has already been removed from the published cache.' Then explains: 'contentCache.GetById(item.Id) returns null because the page is no longer in the cache, the if (soonToBeUnPublishedItem != null) guard skips the item, and nothing is ever added.'

expectations.text: The agent states that the comment in the copied code (that the item is still in the cache) is wrong for this notification
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states: 'The comment in the docs sample is wrong for v17. It says "item being unpublished will still be in the cache, as unpublishing event fires before the cache is updated". That would be true of the "-ing" notification, but the sample handles the "-ed" one.'

Section heading 'The fix: handle ContentUnpublishingNotification' and the code block shows 'public class HandleUnPublishingHandler : INotificationHandler<ContentUnpublishingNotification>' on line 25 of the response code.

expectations.text: The fix reads the URL from the published cache via EnsureUmbracoContext() in a using (injecting the singleton IPublishedContentCache, available in Umbraco 15+, and looking up per call is equally acceptable)
expectations.evidence: Code block (lines 44-49) shows: 'using UmbracoContextReference contextReference = _umbracoContextFactory.EnsureUmbracoContext();' followed by 'IPublishedContent? published = contextReference.UmbracoContext.Content?.GetById(item.Key);'. This implements the 'looking up per call' variant which is stated as equally acceptable in the expectation. The note section confirms this is valid: 'Your GetById(item.Id) and .Url() also work inside the using.'

expectations.text: The handler registration is updated to the -ing notification with builder.AddNotificationHandler
expectations.evidence: Response includes code: 'builder.AddNotificationHandler<ContentUnpublishingNotification, HandleUnPublishingHandler>();' on line 64, with context that states: 'If you only change the class, the handler is still registered against the old notification type and won't compile. In your composer (or in Program.cs)' showing the registration is updated to ContentUnpublishingNotification.

expectations.text: If no buildable project is available, the agent does not claim the fix was compiled or run
expectations.evidence: Response section 'Things to check afterwards' states: 'I couldn't run this against your site, so it isn't verified for your project.' This directly acknowledges no compilation or runtime verification was done.

eval_feedback.overall: All expectations are well-validated against the response. The eval set is comprehensive and each assertion maps to a key part of the diagnosis and fix. The response demonstrates clear understanding of the notification lifecycle issue, identifies the exact problem, provides working code, and appropriately disclaims that the fix was not tested against the user's actual project.
